gh:#177 https://github.com/theodoreOnzGit/outram-park-backend/issues/177

Godiva +57, Jemima +6, HEU-SOL-THERM-009 -18 pcm all passed while the code was
+2950 pcm on LEU-COMP-THERM-008. Self-shielded resonance absorption needs a
moderator AND a large U-238 share AND lumped fuel, all at once; the three passing
cases each miss one. ACTION: record the mechanism-coverage matrix in
VERIFICATION_AND_VALIDATION.md; each new benchmark must name the mechanism it is
first to reach; holes are a Pu-239 thermal lattice, a graphite-moderated LEU case
with an external answer, and a fast LEU lattice. Data blocker: N-14 (FENDL is in
git-annex; NNDC/IAEA are 403 here).

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
CONCRETE INSTANCE, 2026-09-12: op-0iaq / gh:#193. The +4000 pcm FHR ring-RPT residual was a threshold reaction with a non-zero cross section BELOW its threshold, and it fired on exactly one nuclide -- F-19 -- because F-19 is the only evaluation in this repo's reference data that opens a threshold MF=3 section above zero (MT=51 at 0.018129 b, MT=52 at 0.0042683 b; every other nuclide's threshold sections start at 0.0 b).

The coverage table classified the FHR pebble as 'thermal + graphite-moderated + heterogeneous', every axis of which had another representative (HTR-10, LCT-008, HST-009, Godiva). The axis that actually mattered -- 'the only case whose moderator contains fluorine' -- was not an axis anyone had written down, because nothing suggested fluorine was a mechanism.

The lesson as stated (cover by MECHANISM) is right but understates the problem: the mechanism here was not a physics mechanism at all, it was a DATA-SHAPE mechanism (does this evaluation open its threshold sections at zero?). A coverage table indexed on reactor physics could not have contained it. What found it was pricing mechanisms by switching them off until one nuclide's channel accounted for the whole residual.

title: Lesson: benchmark coverage by MECHANISM, not spectrum label

description: Confirmed real bug: EntityConfig::paper() defaults new papers to Classification::unsorted() (topics=['unsorted']), but no topics/unsorted/kovan.toml directory is ever created, so KnowledgeIndex::children_of('') never surfaces it and an unclassified paper is currently invisible in the Wiki browser -- papers_in('unsorted') would find it, but nothing lets the user navigate there. Add a synthetic 'Unsorted' entry at the Wiki root (shown whenever index.papers_in("unsorted") is non-empty) that sets current='unsorted' on click, reusing the existing drill-down/papers_in machinery -- no new collection directory needed.

description:
Terry et al. (2005) section 2, quoted in
crates/kovan-literature/derived/terry2005-htr10-rz-zone-geometry.md:256-257:

  'the conus and discharge tube contained only dummy pebbles'

The conus was modelled as part of the bed hex lattice, which applies the
core's 57:43 fuel:dummy split everywhere. So the conus was filled with FUEL
pebbles. That is why modelling it was worth +4578 +/- 158 pcm and overshot RMC
by 5x: the geometry was right, the CONTENTS were not.

Consequence for the record: the earlier -909 pcm (flat-bottomed bed) was NOT
missing 13.6 % of the model's fuel. It was missing the conus's DUMMY pebbles
and had reflector graphite in their place -- a far smaller perturbation. The
'two offsetting errors' reading of -909 pcm is itself suspect and must be
re-examined once the conus carries the right contents.

Same for the discharge tube: dummy pebbles, not solid reflector graphite
(what the model had) and not helium (the bounding ablation run here).

FIX: assign every lattice level below the bed bottom the dummy universe, and
model the discharge tube as homogenised dummy pebbles.
title: HTR-10 conus was filled with FUEL pebbles; Terry says dummy pebbles only
